blocks.text: Mastering browser navigation for IT support

Efficiency in technical support depends on how fast you move between tabs. When you have a ticketing system, a remote dashboard, and a documentation wiki open, clicking is too slow. Use ⌘ + T to open a new tab. Use ⌘ + Option + Right Arrow to cycle through your open tabs. If you need to find a specific tab among fifty, press ⌘ + Shift + A to open the tab search box. Type the name of the system you need and hit Enter.

When a user reports that a web portal is broken, do not clear all browser data immediately. This forces you to re-authenticate everywhere. Instead, clear site data for that one domain. Click the lock icon in the address bar, then select Site Settings. Look for the Usage section and click Clear data. This keeps your other sessions intact while fixing the local cache issues.
Using Chrome profiles for different clients

If you support multiple clients, use separate Chrome profiles. Each profile acts as a clean browser instance. Go to your profile icon in the top right, then click Add. This keeps cookies, saved passwords, and extensions isolated. You will never accidentally log into a client portal using your own credentials.
Essential keyboard shortcuts for Mac technicians

items: ⌘ + L: Jump to the address bar to type a new URL or search query.
⌘ + Shift + N: Open a new Incognito window for testing site access without extensions.
⌘ + Option + I: Open Developer Tools to inspect console errors for a failing page.
⌘ + R: Reload the current page ignoring the cache.
⌘ + Shift + Delete: Open the clear browsing data menu.

blocks.text: Extensions are useful, but they eat memory. Technical support specialists should audit their extensions monthly. Go to chrome://extensions to see what is running. If you do not use it daily, remove it. Use the pinning feature to keep only your essential tools visible in the toolbar. This prevents clutter and keeps your browser lean.

If Chrome feels sluggish, check the Task Manager by pressing Shift + Esc. It shows exactly which tab or extension is consuming your CPU or RAM. End the process there rather than restarting the whole browser.
blocks.title: Stop slow tabs fast

blocks.text: Writing the same resolution steps repeatedly is a waste of time. Use a text expander or the built-in dictation features on your Mac. When you use Lazur, you can hold the fn key and dictate your notes directly into your web-based ticketing system. It formats your speech into clean text, allowing you to close the ticket and move to the next one without manual typing.

Never save client passwords in your personal browser profile. Use a dedicated business password manager. Ensure that Enhanced Safe Browsing is enabled in Settings > Privacy and security > Security. This gives you real-time protection against malicious sites that might be hosting phishing attempts.

faq.question: How do I check my current Chrome version on Mac?
faq.answer: Click the Chrome menu in the top bar, then select About Google Chrome. It will display your current version and check for updates.

faq.question: Can I use Chrome on older versions of macOS?
faq.answer: Google Chrome requires macOS 13 Ventura or later for current updates. Older systems are capped at version 138.

faq.question: How can I quickly find a specific menu item in Chrome settings?
faq.answer: Use the search bar at the top of the Settings page. Type the feature name, like 'cookies' or 'passwords', to jump directly to that section.
